scope: Source labels/format and first-three-record previews only; no site sampling, temporal interpolation, spatial validation or boundary selection

interpretation.PCP: Multi-year bolometric brightness averages binned by season and subsolar longitude; empty spatial bins omitted; not a mission-day equipment temperature
interpretation.PRP: Model-calculated annual average at 2 cm, annual surface maximum and ice-stability depth; not instantaneous measurements or confirmed ice; exclusion value -999 applies to ice depth

products.table_description:
This table contains bolometric brightness 
        temperatures from the Diviner Lunar Radiometer
        Experiment binned at 240 m resolution derived
        from a compilation of all nadir observations
        acquired from 5-July-2009 to 15-March-2020
        with ecliptic longitude (L_s) 0 to 60 degrees and
        subsolar longitude 0 to 15 degrees. Columns are 
        distances from pole (x,y) normalized by mean radius
        1737.4 km, longitude, latitude, local time, 
        bolometric temperature. Empty bins are omitted.
        For more information, please see:
        Schorghofer and Williams (2020) 'Mapping of ice storage 
        processes on the Moon with time-dependent temperatures', 
        PSJ, 1, 54, https://doi.org/10.3847/PSJ/abb6ff.

fields.name: ice_depth
fields.description:
The calculated depth at which water ice would be
                        sublimated at a rate of 1 kg m-2 per billion years
                        (m). Notes: If the calculated depth at which water
                        ice would be sublimated at a rate of 1 kg m-2 per
                        billion years is zero, then water ice is stable to
                        sublimation at the surface. Also, if the
                        calculated depth at which water ice would be
                        sublimated at a rate of 1 kg m-2 per billion years
                        is greater than 2.8738 meters, then the exclude
                        value of -999.0 is reported.
